Mitochondrial and nuclear markers identified 8 Trichuris trichiura infections. Those findings broaden the recognized host range of this human soil-transmitted helminth and raise questions regarding wildlife involvement in its transmission ecology.

items.summary_en: In 2024, we detected Mycobacterium ulcerans DNA in 2 of 46 fruit bats in Akonolinga, Cameroon, whereas 111 aquatic macroinvertebrate pools were negative for M. ulcerans. Broader longitudinal surveillance will be needed to clarify the role of fruit bats as a reservoir for M. ulcerans circulation in Cameroon and Africa.

items.summary_en: We report a case of Armillifer armillatus infection in Arras, France, in a woman originally from the Democratic Republic of the Congo. She manifested abdominal pain that mimicked a strangulated umbilical hernia. Clinicians should be aware of this parasitic infection, particularly in patients with a history of snake exposure.

items.summary_en: We report a case of Neoehrlichia mikurensis infection from a tick bite in a 69-year-old immunocompromised man with non-Hodgkin lymphoma in the Netherlands. Because of increasing use of immunosuppressive therapies and frequent tick bites, N. mikurensis should be recognized as a potential cause of recurrent fever in immunocompromised patients.

items.summary_en: Spillover of influenza A(H5N1) virus to cattle in the United States sparked global concern. We investigated whether endemic avian influenza viruses are potentially spilling over into domestic livestock in Egypt. We detected influenza H9N2 antibodies in 2.5% and H5N1 antibodies in 2.9%-4.5% of tested animals. Additional surveillance will elucidate host infection dynamics.

items.summary_en: Porcine deltacoronavirus (PDCoV) is a swine coronavirus with zoonotic potential. We detected PDCoV-neutralizing antibodies in 10 of 300 human serum samples; positive sample sources included 1 adult and 9 juveniles. Our findings provide evidence of human exposure to PDCoV and highlight the importance of monitoring animal coronaviruses with zoonotic potential.

items.summary_en: We detected disseminated granulomatous disease with abundant acid-fast bacilli in free-ranging, white-nosed coatis in Costa Rica. Molecular characterization identified Mycobacterium africanum lineage 6. Our findings demonstrate the presence of M. africanum in free-ranging wildlife in the Americas and highlight the value of wildlife surveillance for prompting coordinated One Health investigation and response.

items.summary_en: Pet rats represent a reservoir of multiple zoonotic pathogens. We demonstrated that pet rats, previously confirmed to be Seoul orthohantavirus-infected and involved in human infections in Germany, were concurrently infected with rat hepatitis E virus. The high degree of rat hepatitis E virus sequence identity suggests a single incursion event.

items.summary_en: Livestock-associated Staphylococcus aureus caused 200 human bloodstream infections in Denmark during 2007-2023; two thirds were caused by methicillin-susceptible isolates. Risk for death was comparable to that associated with human S. aureus clones. Industrial pig population size correlated strongly with disease prevalence. Seventeen percent of isolates showed signs of human adaptation.

All samples were negative for dengue, Chikungunya, and Zika virus. One imported Oropouche virus infection was detected.

items.summary_en: Mayaro virus (MAYV) is an emerging pathogen in Latin America. Using phylodynamic reconstructions and phylowave analyses, we describe novel lineage diversification and rapid dispersal of MAYV in Peru. A newly developed, dual-target quantitative reverse transcription PCR assay reliably detects MAYV variants, enabling improved surveillance, control, and understanding of this neglected arbovirus.

items.summary_en: Oropouche fever emerged nationwide in Cuba in 2024. We investigated the outbreak in Havana; of 549 suspected cases, 189 (34.4%) were confirmed. No cases were severe. Incidence was 8.9/100,000 population and was highest in adults 27-59 years of age (10.2/100,000 population). Three infants tested positive. Dengue cocirculation challenged surveillance.
